title: Rational Design of TDP-43 Derived alpha-Helical Peptide Inhibitors: An In Silico Strategy to Prevent TDP-43 Aggregation in Neurodegenerative Disorders.
authors: Salaikumaran, Muthu Raj; Gopal, Pallavi P
one_liner_zh: 该文用分子对接和MD模拟设计TDP-43衍生α-螺旋肽抑制剂以阻止其聚集，虽涉及蛋白-DNA结合蛋白但核心是蛋白-蛋白聚集，非TF-DNA互作体系，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: TDP-43, an essential RNA/DNA-binding protein, is central to the pathology of neurodegenerative diseases, such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia. Pathological mislocalization and aggregation of TDP-43 disrupt RNA splicing, mRNA stability, and mRNA transport, thereby impairing neuronal function and survival. The formation of amyloid-like TDP-43 filaments is largely facilitated by the destabilization of an alpha-helical segment within the disordered C-terminal region. In this study, we hypothesized that preventing the destabilization of the alpha-helical domain could potentially halt the growth of these pathological filaments. To explore this, we utilized a range of in silico techniques to design and evaluate peptide-based therapeutics that bind to pathological TDP-43 amyloid-like filament crystal structures and resist beta sheet conversion. Our computational approaches, including biophysical and secondary structure property prediction, molecular docking, 3D structure prediction, and molecular dynamics simulations, were used to assess the structure, stability, and binding affinity of these peptides in relation to pathological TDP-43 filaments. The results of our in silico analyses identified a selection of promising peptides which displayed a stable alpha-helical structure, exhibited an increased number of intramolecular hydrogen bonds within the helical domain, and demonstrated high binding affinities for pathological TDP-43 amyloid-like filaments. Molecular dynamics simulations provided further support for the structural and thermodynamic stability of these peptides, as they exhibited lower root-mean-square deviation and more favorable free energy landscapes over 300 ns. These findings establish alpha-helical propensity peptides as potential lead molecules for the development of novel therapeutics against TDP-43 aggregation. This structure-based computational approach for the rational design of peptide inhibitors opens a new direction in the search for effective interventions for ALS, FTD, and other related neurodegenerative diseases. The peptides identified as the most promising candidates in this study are currently subject to further testing and validation through both in vitro and in vivo experiments.
abstract_zh: TDP-43，一种必需的RNA/DNA结合蛋白，在神经退行性疾病（如肌萎缩侧索硬化症和额颞叶痴呆）的病理过程中扮演核心角色。病理性的错误定位和TDP-43聚集破坏了RNA剪接、mRNA稳定性及mRNA运输，从而损害神经元功能与存活。淀粉样样TDP-43纤维的形成主要得益于无序C末端区域内α-螺旋片段的不稳定化。在本研究中，我们假设阻止α-螺旋结构域的不稳定化可能潜在地阻止这些病理性纤维的生长。为探索此假设，我们利用一系列计算机模拟技术设计并评估了与病理性TDP-43淀粉样样纤维晶体结构结合并抵抗β折叠转化的肽类治疗剂。我们的计算方法，包括生物物理和二级结构性质预测、分子对接、三维结构预测及分子动力学模拟，被用于评估这些肽相对于病理性TDP-43纤维的结构、稳定性和结合亲和力。我们的计算机分析结果识别出一批有前景的肽，它们展现出稳定的α-螺旋结构，螺旋结构域内分子内氢键数量增加，并对病理性TDP-43淀粉样样纤维表现出高结合亲和力。分子动力学模拟进一步支持了这些肽的结构和热力学稳定性，因为它们在300纳秒内表现出较低的均方根偏差和更有利的自由能景观。这些发现确立了具有α-螺旋倾向性的肽作为开发针对TDP-43聚集的新型治疗剂的潜在先导分子。这种基于结构的计算策略用于合理设计肽抑制剂，为寻找针对ALS、FTD及其他相关神经退行性疾病的有效干预措施开辟了新方向。本研究中识别为最有前景候选物的肽目前正通过体外和体内实验进行进一步测试和验证。
